description: A long H3 take of one speaker held to a retimed narration, a segment per line, probed then continued. The narration is made first with templates/narration-retime, whose 'num_frames' and 'guide_frames' must equal this template's (192 and 22 by default), or the segment boundaries land in the wrong places; listen to the retimed track before spending GPU time on it, and pass it as 'narration' and the same text as 'script'. The first step (narration_lines) cuts the narration at the chain's own segment boundaries and fills 'prompt_template' once per segment with that segment's line and 'scene', 'speaker' and 'soundscape', so the plan derives the segment count from the narration's length; the 'take' step is a guide chain matched to the narration and holding it as the soundtrack, so the speech heard is the narration itself and the guide carries picture only. 'prompt_template' takes bare placeholders ({line}, {scene}, {speaker}, {soundscape}); write a literal brace doubled. Its default has no spoken cue and no breath: the held narration already starts each segment mid-sentence. What it holds, measured (bench/records/narrated.md, 12 segments of about 86 s at tier best): the narration is held unbroken under every 'shot'. 'shot' 'dialogue' (the default) etches the face by about 30 s and steps face_drop up at segment 6 (36 s), so it suits a take of about 30 s (4 segments). 'shot' 'standing' holds face and backdrop to about 85 s with face_drop within 0.015 (seed 1 only), with no keyframes: she stands, and each segment eases back to the opening frame. 'shot' 'walk_keyframed' holds the face to 85 s (face_drop at most 0.041 on two seeds) and moves, at the price of a hand-built keyframe per segment. Nothing is measured past 86 s, and no 'shot' cleared face, lip sync and motion together at 86 s. A piece longer than one clean take is split into passages, one narrated take per passage with its own narration-retime and its own opening still, joined as cuts (not yet run end to end). Wall time measured: about 18-19 min per segment on dialogue and walk_keyframed; standing took 282 min for 12 segments (about 23.5, with two re-rolls), at tier best on an RTX 3090. The procedure: first validate with 'stop_after' set for a probe, k = (the seconds the 'shot' holds) / ((num_frames - guide_frames) / 24): 4 for 'dialogue', up to 12 for 'standing' (a whole number; the estimate prices only the k segments it renders). Run the probe and judge its segments with get_output_frames and compare_outputs, and read each shot's check values (face_drop is recorded, never failed, since 'check' leaves its ceiling null). If the probe holds, run again with 'resume_from' set to the output: reference of the probe's last kept segment file and 'stop_after' cleared to null, which renders only the segments after it; a bad segment is re-rendered in place with templates/minimax/repair-segment ('keep_segments' stays true for that). Judge lip sync by eye on the finished take, or with the measure_lip_sync task; the chain's check does not measure it, and it holds no words check, since the held audio is the narration itself. 'shot' has three presets: 'dialogue' (guide continuity, the default), 'standing' (guide continuity with keystone 'segment_1' at keystone_slot 'last' and no keyframes) and 'walk_keyframed' (the same keystone with keyframes), the moving keystone: pass 'keyframes', a list of stills one per segment (or one previous_result: list of them), and segment k ends on keyframe k as its last image, so the camera moves and the face holds (docs/proposals/complete/narrated-long-take-complete.md, Amendment 1). Each keyframe needs an open, mid-word mouth, since a closed-mouth keyframe drops lip sync at the segment's end, and a keyframe face that differs from the still is followed and accumulates; a walk did not read at chest-up framing and a slow lateral camera arc did. Draw the keyframes from the speaker still (FLUX 3 Klein edit) and review them before any video is rendered: an inconsistent series shows as a pulse at every segment end. 'keyframes' (default null, off) needs 'shot' 'walk_keyframed' (or keystone 'segment_1' with keystone_slot 'last') and at least one keyframe per planned segment, the full take's even for a probe; it is refused otherwise. 'tier' 'best' (the default) is 1344x768 on int8 weights and 'standard' 960x544 on int4, both at 20 steps with no turbo LoRA ('lora_model_name' null), since the turbo LoRA flattens H3 voices and lip sync. Keep 'num_frames' on H3's 3-frame audio grid (141, 192, 243, 294, 345) or validate warns that the held slices drift. No cost row: the figure above is wall time at one tier, not a calibrated row.

vram_estimate.reason: each segment is one H3 run, so the ceiling is a segment's: the t2va calibration (#324) - peak activation memory scales with width * height * num_frames - plus, under 'guide' continuity, the guide each segment after the first is given, which is encoded on the target canvas and costs about as much per voxel as the clip itself (docs/proposals/h3-guide-vram.md, #694)

variables.soundscape: Quiet natural ambience under the voice: a soft steady breeze and faint distant birdsong, with no other voices.
variables.prompt_template:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, cinematic, photorealistic, one continuous shot that carries over without a break from the previous shot. The shot opens exactly on <Picture 1>: {scene} Preserving the speaker's face, clothing, framing and the setting exactly, the camera holds its framing for the whole shot: it never pushes in, and the speaker stays the same size in frame from the first frame to the last. (S1), {speaker}, at the same quiet level and unhurried pace as before, is already speaking and continues mid-flow, lips and jaw shaping every word clearly and in time with the sound: <d>[English] {line}</d> The delivery carries straight on to the end of the shot, with no pause to start over.

overall_soundscape: {soundscape} The ambience runs under the voice throughout and never drops out.

non_diegetic_music: N/A

image.reason: the speaker's first frame, <Picture 1> of every segment prompt; a placeholder would film the wrong person

narration.reason: the retimed narration from templates/narration-retime, the take's held soundtrack and the source of its segment count; there is no sensible default track

script.reason: the text the narration speaks, so each segment's line carries its spelling and punctuation

scene.reason: the shot's framing, the speaker's look and the setting, written for this take; a placeholder would describe another scene

speaker.reason: the speaker's voice and delivery for the (S1) tag; a placeholder would describe another voice

num_frames.reason: the video VAE encodes 17 * n + 5 frames, and MiniMax-H3 generates between 5 and 15 seconds at 24 fps

width.reason: MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses a `width` or `height` that is not a multiple of 32, and only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for

height.reason: MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses a `width` or `height` that is not a multiple of 32, and only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for
